research_question: Under what evidentiary conditions can IG 2.0 reconstruct institutional arrangements from public records of decentralized coordination?
design: Purposive comparative episode study with evidence availability modeling; not a randomized benchmark or a population estimate.
selection_rules: Exclude all 24 previous focal episodes and bridge 15626.
Screen titles and source lengths first; select historical and outcome variation with manageable full discussions.
Retain thin records and contrary cases; disclose any content-informed selection.
Group linked episodes rather than claiming independent observations.

evidence_layers.D: Contemporaneous dated standing guidance only. Proposed documents separately labeled and not treated as standing.
evidence_layers.T: D plus complete available frozen discussion and recorded outcome.
evidence_layers.I: T plus relevant commit-pinned files, patches, and implementation evidence.

execution: One continuing assistant analysis, with deterministic exact-evidence checks and a separate within-session source review. No independent or blind model runs are claimed. Evidence-layer comparisons are source-availability assessments, not performance estimates.
coding_scope: Focal institutional propositions and case mechanisms, applying v0.3 distinctions. Complete packets retained and read; not exhaustive v0.3 component annotation of every candidate statement.
narrative_comparison: Within-session structured versus narrative representation on selected contrasts; a diagnostic of information preservation, not a blind efficacy benchmark.
primary_outputs: Focal claim ledger with source anchors and counterevidence
Mechanism maps and bounded level conclusions
known_limits: Public corpus may omit patch histories, comment edits, thread links, and off-platform activity.
No model accuracy, superiority, cost or scalability estimates.
Recorded merges do not establish recognition of each provision or network adoption.
Source sufficiency remains revisable; richer evidence is not a gold standard.
